text:
Marathon Petroleum stock fell 2.3% today after climbing sharply over the past two days, as crude oil prices retreated on October 15th despite ongoing Middle East tensions. The company benefits when oil prices rise—refiners buy cheap crude and sell refined products like gasoline and diesel at higher margins—but today's pullback in crude (down from recent highs) and the cautious market mood around Hormuz shipping attacks weighed on the stock after yesterday's 1.6% gain.

The broader context is volatile: over two weeks MPC is still up 12.7%, riding a wave of geopolitical risk premium as Iran escalates attacks on ships and Saudi facilities. That risk premium cooled slightly today as traders digested the real impact of the disruptions, but with refineries running at 92.7% capacity and inventories moderate, the refining sector remains supported by tight supply conditions.
